toolsets.name: core
toolsets.description: Always-on diagnostics and toolset management.

toolsets.name: inspection
toolsets.description: Read-only project, scene, and node inspection.

toolsets.name: scene_edit
toolsets.description: Create, modify, and delete nodes, scripts, signals, and scenes (mutating + destructive).

toolsets.name: runtime
toolsets.description: Run the project headless and capture its output/errors.

toolsets.name: scripts
toolsets.description: Read, write, and patch GDScript files; check for parse errors.

toolsets.name: resources_edit
toolsets.description: Read/create/edit resource (.tres) files and register autoloads.

toolsets.name: project
toolsets.description: Explore the filesystem, search files, read/write project settings, resolve UIDs.

toolsets.name: editor
toolsets.description: Capture editor screenshots (image content for vision-capable clients).

toolsets.name: physics
toolsets.description: Configure physics bodies, collision shapes, layers/masks, and raycasts.

toolsets.name: animation
toolsets.description: Author animations (tracks/keyframes) and AnimationTree state machines/blend trees.

toolsets.name: scene_3d
toolsets.description: Build 3D scenes: mesh instances, cameras, lights, WorldEnvironment, and GridMap cells.

toolsets.name: particles
toolsets.description: Create/configure GPU particle systems: process material, color gradients, and VFX presets.

toolsets.name: navigation
toolsets.description: Author navigation: regions, agents, navmesh baking, and navigation layers.

toolsets.name: audio
toolsets.description: Set up audio: stream players, audio bus layout, and bus effects.

toolsets.name: tilemap
toolsets.description: Edit TileMap/TileMapLayer cells: set, fill rect, get, clear, list layers.

toolsets.name: theme_ui
toolsets.description: Create themes and override colors, font sizes, and styleboxes on Control nodes.

toolsets.name: shader
toolsets.description: Author shaders: create/read shader files, assign ShaderMaterial, set shader parameters.

toolsets.name: input_map
toolsets.description: Edit the project's Input Map actions and events (add/remove/clear).

toolsets.name: input
toolsets.description: Drive a running game: synthesize key/mouse/action input and play input sequences (needs a play session + runtime probe).

toolsets.name: testing
toolsets.description: Automated play-testing: run scenarios, assert live node state, diff screenshots, and fuzz with random input.

toolsets.name: profiling
toolsets.description: Read Godot performance monitors (FPS, draw calls, memory, physics) for the editor or a running game.

toolsets.name: batch
toolsets.description: Operate over many nodes/scenes: find by type, batch-set a property, cross-scene edits, and dependency analysis.

toolsets.name: analysis
toolsets.description: Static project analysis: unused resources, signal flow, circular script dependencies, and scene-complexity stats.

toolsets.name: export
toolsets.description: Drive the export pipeline: list presets, report export info, and run an export (needs export templates).

toolsets.name: debugger
toolsets.description: Debugger breakpoint control: set, remove, clear breakpoints and force breaks in a running game (needs a play session).

toolsets.name: asset_import
toolsets.description: Import external assets (local files or URLs) into the project and assemble PBR materials from textures.

toolsets.name: visual_shader
toolsets.description: Create and edit Visual Shader node graphs: create shaders, add nodes, wire connections, and set node parameters.

toolsets.name: project_scaffold
toolsets.description: Generate a project skeleton (directories, settings, autoloads, root scene) for common game types so agents start from a known structure.

toolsets.name: composite
toolsets.description: Macro tools that collapse multi-step scene edits into one atomic, single-undo round-trip (compose a node with script/children, batch-create nodes, apply many edits at once). Individual scene_edit tools still work.

common_errors.cause: The toolset containing that tool is not enabled.
common_errors.fix: Call godot_list_toolsets, then godot_enable_toolset("scene_edit") (or the relevant category) before using the tool.

common_errors.cause: Godot is not running or the addon is not enabled.
common_errors.fix: Open Godot with the project and enable the addon in Project Settings.

common_errors.cause: No .tscn scene is open in the editor.
common_errors.fix: Open a scene file in Godot, or call godot_scene_edit_create_scene(root_type=…, scene_path=…) to make one (enable the scene_edit toolset first).

common_errors.cause: Destructive tool (godot_scene_edit_delete_node, godot_scene_edit_reload_scene) needs explicit confirmation.
common_errors.fix: Add confirm=True to the call, or use dry_run=True to preview first.

common_errors.cause: Live runtime/input tools need an active editor play session.
common_errors.fix: Call play_scene() first, and ensure the runtime probe autoload is registered.

common_errors.cause: The game was launched from the editor but lacks the MCPRuntimeProbe autoload.
common_errors.fix: Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in Project Settings.

common_errors.cause: The connected Godot editor is older than the toolset's minimum.
A node, scene, script, or resource path does not exist.
common_errors.fix: Verify the path with get_scene_tree() or get_filesystem_tree() first.

Yes, Godot is connected. The server and the editor addon are both version 2026.10.15, linked over `ws://localhost:9080`, with no version mismatch. I only read from the project and changed nothing.

## Project
- **Name:** MCP Lab Platformer
- **Godot:** 4.7.2-stable (official)
- **Main scene:** `res://scenes/level.tscn`, which is open and active in the editor
- **Scenes:** `level.tscn` and `player.tscn`
- **Autoload:** `McpRuntimeProbe` is already registered, so we can run the game from the editor and test it live
- **Custom input actions:** `move_left`, `move_right`, `jump` (everything else is Godot's built-in `ui_*` actions)

## Scene tree (`level.tscn`)
```
Level (Node2D)
├── Floor (StaticBody2D) @ (600, 620)
│   ├── Look (ColorRect) 1200×40, slate blue
│   └── CollisionShape2D
├── Ledge (StaticBody2D) @ (300, 260)
│   ├── Look (ColorRect) 240×24, same color
│   └── CollisionShape2D
├── Coins (Node2D)
│   ├── Coin1 (ColorRect) 16×16 gold @ (640, 520)
│   ├── Coin2 (ColorRect) 16×16 gold @ (800, 480)
│   └── Coin3 (ColorRect) 16×16 gold @ (960, 520)
└── Player (CharacterBody2D, instance of player.tscn, script res://scripts/player.gd) @ (300, 220)
    ├── Body (ColorRect) 24×40, blue
    └── CollisionShape2D
```

## Things I noticed
- **Simple shapes only:** everything is drawn with plain colored rectangles. There are no sprites, tilemaps, camera or UI.
- **Coins can't be collected yet:** each coin is just a colored rectangle. None of them has an area or collision shape, and no script is attached, so touching one does nothing.
- **Player start:** the player starts just above the Ledge (feet at y=240, ledge top at y=248), so it should drop a few pixels onto it when the game starts.
- **Player settings:** `player.gd` doesn't expose any editable settings in the editor. I haven't read the script itself yet because that needs the `scripts` toolset.
- **Not checked yet:** I haven't looked at the collision shapes' sizes or the game camera settings.

To read `player.gd` or check for errors, I'd turn on the `scripts` toolset next (that only reads). To start making changes, I'd add `scene_edit`.
